label: AMK / Kartel Music Group
release_notes: Lineup now: Charlie Drinkwater - vocals; Alex Sprogis - guitar, with a wider circle of collaborators on piano, fiddle, manipulated birdsong, programmed drums and a dance-influenced low end. Bassist/keyboardist Nic Bueth and drummer Ed Kelland, on the first two albums, are listed as past members (Wikipedia).

Producer, studio and mastering are not published. Genius credits Love Song (A Good Kind of Weapon) to Sprogis, Murray Matravers and Simon Tyrie. Matravers fronts the band Easy Life and is credited as a producer and engineer (AllMusic); no other credits found for Tyrie.

Lineage: London, formed 2019 by four friends who made music together as teenagers (Sub Pop). Uppers and My Other People were both on Sub Pop, produced by Bueth at Studio East, London. No earlier bands for the members found.
Drinkwater calls the record one about confusion, surveillance and late capitalism. Press sets it beside R.E.M., Radiohead, The National and Foals.

Sound across the singles: breakbeat drums, spoken word and data samples on The Mud Never Dries; strings, synths and a more sung vocal on Love Song (A Good Kind of Weapon); cantering guitar riffs on Cartoons (press coverage).

pull_quotes.text: containing some of TV Priest’s most potent melodies to date

draft_comment: Post-punk with the doors thrown open: strings, fiddle, breakbeats and birdsong. Out Nov. 6, so most of the FCC screen is still open.

tracks.title: Just So You Know
tracks.notes: Opens on solemn strings, then turns into a groove-heavy, muscular indie rocker (press coverage). All-out blaster (Clash). Breakup song in which the other party is technology (Drinkwater)

tracks.title: Cartoons
tracks.notes: Cantering, fleet-footed guitar riffs (press coverage). Drinkwater calls it a summary of the album, a simpler shape built on hooks

tracks.title: The Mud Never Dries
tracks.notes: Cold start on a breakbeat blast of programmed drums, then a restless, propulsive bassline and fractured post-punk (Clash, Rockshot). Spoken word over rising electronic noise near the end. Band: drum and bass, post-punk, data samples, spoken word. Their most abrasive song (Drinkwater)

tracks.title: Love Song (A Good Kind of Weapon)
tracks.notes: Slow-burning and brooding: strings, shimmering synths and understated electronics under a melodic sung vocal (Rockshot, press coverage). Compared to Radiohead and The National (press coverage). Co-produced by Sprogis, Matravers and Tyrie

sources: Note: Clash's announcement text says Oct. 6 once, but its headline and every other source say Nov. 6. Bandcamp calls The Mud Never Dries the lead single; the announcement press calls Love Song (A Good Kind of Weapon) the lead single.
Lyrics screened (counts only): tracks 1 and 4 on Genius; track 6 on LRCLIB (Genius has no lyrics yet). Track 2 has no lyrics on Genius or LRCLIB. Tracks 3, 5 and 7 to 10 are unreleased.
